answer: An agent archive stores quill drawings of opal deposits in a canyon. Storage providers gain weight only by proving retention of uniquely encoded replicas bound to their keys and registered replica IDs. Unpredictable spot checks with short deadlines make regenerating missing replicas impractical. Each replica counts once, so aliases need additional physical storage to gain weight, not merely new names. This requires a sound proof-of-replication scheme and does not stop large storage owners.
